data.name: Kripal
data.gender_notes: Kripal is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'kripa', meaning 'cruelty' or 'wickedness'. In Hindu mythology, the demon Kripalasura is known for his cruel and deceitful nature. He was killed by Lord Rama, but his name continues to symbolize mischief and trickery. The name Kripal carries the meaning “Cruel, Wicked, Trickster” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kripal usually hope their child will grow to embody cruel, wicked, trickster and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Kripal belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Cruel, Wicked, Trickster.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kripal total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Kripal" carries a negative connotation in Hindu culture due to its association with the demon Kripalasura. It may not be a popular choice for parents when naming their children due to the undesirable secondary meaning associated with it.
data.spiritual_significance: Despite the negative connotation, the name "Kripal" can have a deeper spiritual significance in the context of the Hindu spiritual tradition. In Hindu mythology, Lord Vishnu is known to have the power of 'krpalu', or mercy and compassion. One can view the name "Kripal" as a reminder to cultivate and practice the virtue of mercy, in the face of temptation to resort to cruelty and deceitfulness. It is a call to awaken the warrior within to conquer our inner demons and sow the seeds of kindness and compassion instead.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Kripal signifies the embodiment of compassion and mischief, where the divine play of life unfolds with both love and trickery. It is a reminder that even in the face of adversity, the universe is always playing a cosmic game of hide-and-seek, guiding us towards our highest potential.

The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
